// Part: grounds (stub: its worker fills in build(g)).
export function build(g) {}
// The site grid in WORLD coordinates (plan.md): x 0..38, y -5..28, z 0..32. The toolkit's Grid only takes y >= 0 and
// load() reads only that, so the grid stores y + YOFF internally and save() writes the file in that shifted frame.
// Parts, runParts and sockets.json all keep world coordinates.
import { Grid } from "/Volumes/ext1/swe/repos/minecraft-design/tools/src/structure.mjs";

export const SIZE = [39, 34, 33];   // x 0..38, y -5..28, z 0..32 (the file's extent, not world numbers)
export const YOFF = 5;              // world y -5 is file y 0

export class SiteGrid extends Grid {
  constructor() { super(SIZE); }
  /** World bounds: x and z as the file, y from -YOFF up to the top. */
  inBounds(x, y, z) { return x >= 0 && z >= 0 && x < SIZE[0] && z < SIZE[2] && y >= -YOFF && y < SIZE[1] - YOFF; }
  /** Write the structure file, shifted so every y is >= 0. */
  save(path) {
    const out = new Grid(SIZE, { dataVersion: this.dataVersion });
    for (const c of this) out.set(c.pos[0], c.pos[1] + YOFF, c.pos[2], c.block, c.state, c.nbt);
    return out.save(path);
  }
}

input.summary:
grounds part built: three rear yards (yard() at a=25/13/1 with doors 35/23/3) and four lamp posts on the kerb at x 1, 13, 25, 37 (z 5, dark oak fence y 2..4, lantern y 5).
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt; grounds line shows 312 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; lamp posts and yard cells verified in the saved file.
The street (road, kerb, sidewalk) is already laid by parts/shell.mjs, so grounds adds nothing there.
left: Street edging ticks in elements.md belong to the shell: its road, kerb and sidewalk are built, but the item also names the lamp posts, which are now placed (I ticked only the yard item).
`mcd check` reports 3 orphan smooth_stone_slab blocks at (31,6,9), (19,6,9) and (11,6,9). They are not in my part; the frontage or shell should remove or attach them.

Yards have no planting: no shrubs, flowers or trees. The spec only asked for the grass, coarse-dirt patches, path and walls, and the concept shows more planting. I did not add any since it was outside my spec.

The render sheets show no roofs yet (roof part not merged), so the street view has not been checked for lamp-post silhouette against the finished frontage. The lamp posts were checked in a close zoom.

waste.what: Checking that the lamp posts and yard cells landed was a hand-written node script that loads build.nbt and prints block ids cell by cell.
waste.cost: one script, one retry on the import path; about 5 coordinate lists typed by hand
waste.tool: mcd plan or mcd check with a --at cell list (print the block at each coordinate) would have answered this without a script.

waste.what: parts-report shows 'refused 0' for grounds, but the helpers skip non-air cells silently (yard cells over chimney footings, lamp posts blocked by frontage). Those skips are only visible in the helper's returned object, which runParts does not report.
waste.cost: not measured; I had to infer skips by reading the cells back
waste.tool: runParts report should count the helper's skipped list per part, or a `mcd diff`-style check listing planned cells that did not land.

waste.what: Yard and lamp coordinates were copied from plan.md by eye (door x 35/23/3, lamp x list) rather than from one table in the kit.
waste.tool: a shared coordinates JSON (houses, doors, lamp x) imported by every part would remove the copy.

companions.task: plant the yards: a few shrubs or azalea beds on the grass, flower pots by the yard walls, and a planted bed along the yard fence, drawn as a layers() grid so the ground patches read as planting rather than flat grass.
check the kerb and sidewalk junction at the lamp posts (stone-brick kerb course against the polished andesite) and the yard wall copings on x 1, 13, 25, 37.
